tool_args.rationale: The opposing-step signature and varying H make a normalized before/after relaxation plausible, but only five rows are available and the stated target horizon is 0.65, far longer than the 0.004 characteristic tau scale. A short-horizon fit could therefore extrapolate poorly; the available fine trajectory batch is the only relevant probe to improve temporal discrimination before model confirmation.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The 5 observations give a suggestive hysteretic pattern, but they do not establish the relaxation law or distinguish it reliably from other horizon-dependent mechanisms at the required forecast horizon.
The provided rows have no variation in s_grad, so sink coupling is not identifiable; the required slow-horizon discriminating probe is not available in the cost menu.
It is explicitly nuisance data and does not resolve the consequential mechanism ambiguity.
